# Overview

**Module 6: Instability**

This module handles:

1. Reading the settings file: analysis ranges, groups, time, control samples, manual control lengths and exclusions
2. For every measure (each tract and each combined measure), every range and every sample: distribution statistics and modal peaks
3. Group control setpoints, and instability metrics relative to the sample's own setpoint and to its group control
4. All of the above per read and, when UMIs were used, per molecule
5. Comparing tracts (when more than one was measured): whether reads that changed in one tract also changed in the other

**Metric definitions.** Every metric compares each read (or molecule) in a range with a **setpoint**, a reference length for that sample and range (defined below the table). *d* = the read's length minus the setpoint, in repeat units; *n* = how many reads or molecules are in the range. Every column of `instability.xlsx`, with its units, is listed in the workbook's `definitions` sheet.

```{r metric_definitions, results='asis'}
kk <- paste(params$expansion_thresholds, collapse = " and ")
md <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("instability_index", "expansion_index, contraction_index", "mean_change_above_setpoint, mean_change_below_setpoint",
             "share_at_setpoint, share_above_setpoint, share_below_setpoint", sprintf("share_Kplus_above_setpoint, share_Kplus_below_setpoint (K = %s)", kk),
             "n_at_setpoint, n_above_setpoint, n_below_setpoint", "expansion_ratio, contraction_ratio",
             "modal_minus_setpoint, median_minus_setpoint, mean_minus_setpoint"),
  Definition = c("mean(<em>d</em>) &ndash; Lee et al. (2010); positive = longer than the setpoint on average",
                 "sum of the positive (negative) <em>d</em> divided by <em>n</em>, so that instability index = expansion index + contraction index",
                 "mean <em>d</em> among the reads longer (shorter) than the setpoint: how large a typical expansion (contraction) is. Called mean_expansion_size and mean_contraction_size before v3.1, and EI and CI in Duke 2.x",
                 "share of reads at the setpoint (within half a unit), above it, and below it. Called prop_at, prop_above, prop_below before v3.1",
                 "share of reads at least K repeat units above (below) the setpoint. Called prop_above_K, prop_below_K before v3.1",
                 "the same as counts of reads or molecules",
                 "reads above (below) &divide; reads at the setpoint. Kept for continuity, but its denominator is a single length, so it is noisy; <code>share_Kplus_above_setpoint</code> is the stable alternative",
                 "the sample's modal, median or mean length minus the setpoint. Called modal_diff, median_diff, mean_diff before v3.1"))
md$Metric <- vapply(strsplit(md$Metric, ", "), function(x) paste0("<code>", x, "</code>", collapse = ", "), character(1))
md$Metric <- gsub("</code> \\(K = ", " (K = ", md$Metric)
cat(knitr::kable(md, format = "html", escape = FALSE,
                 table.attr = 'class="table table-condensed" style="width:100%; table-layout:auto;"'))
```

The setpoint is the **`r params$control_setpoint_metric`**: the sample's own (`sample_relative`) or the `r params$control_aggregation_method` across its group's control samples (`control_relative`; selection: `r params$control_sample_selection`). Where the settings file gives a manual control length (`manual_control_repeat_length`) for a sample and range, it replaces the group control there; a blank cell uses the group control.

**Outputs:**

- `06_instability/instability.xlsx` – a `definitions` sheet (every column, what it means and its units), ranges, distribution statistics, peaks, controls, instability metrics, tract-comparison statistics
- `06_instability/instability_metrics.tsv` and `distribution_summary.tsv` – the two main tables as plain text, one row per sample, unit, measure and range, for your own analyses in R, Python or Prism
- Every plot file is named `{plot type}_{sample or measure}_{range}_{unit}.png`; the unit is `combined` (reads and molecules in one figure), `reads` or `molecules`, as chosen by `plot_units` (`r paste(plot_units_for(params, isTRUE(params$umi)), collapse = ", ")` in this run)
- `06_instability/plots/` – `counts_per_range_*`, `control_setpoints_*`, `instability_index_by_range_*`, `experiment_map.png`
- `06_instability/plots/timecourse/{unit}/{measure}/` – the headline metrics against time, every measure and every range
- `06_instability/plots/pair_trend/{unit}/{A}_vs_{B}/`, `pair_correlation/…` – tract comparison for every range (`pair_trend_{A}_vs_{B}_{range}_{unit}.png`)
- `06_instability/plots/pair_map/` and `pair_map_group/` – each tract against the other for every read or molecule, all lengths: one figure for the run with a panel per group, and one per group with a panel per sample
- `06_instability/plots/pair_scatter/{reads|molecules}/` – each sample's two tract lengths per read or molecule, one panel per range (`pair_scatter_{sample}_{A}_vs_{B}_{reads|molecules}.png`)

# Settings

```{r load}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
safe_load_module(file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "03_repeat_detection.RData"), 3)
measures <- module3_output$measures; primary <- module3_output$primary
units <- list(reads = module3_output$lengths[, .(file_stem, id = qname, measure, length)])
m4_path <- file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "04_umi.RData")
if (isTRUE(params$umi) && file.exists(m4_path)) {
  safe_load_module(m4_path, 4)
  units$molecules <- module4_output$molecule_lengths[, .(file_stem, id = molecule_id, measure, length)]
}
samples_in_data <- unique(units$reads$file_stem)
# Plots that can show reads and molecules are drawn once per version in plot_units:
# combined (both, in one figure), reads, molecules. The first version is shown in the
# report; every version is saved, with the version at the end of the file name
have_mol <- "molecules" %in% names(units)
unit_title <- c(combined = "reads and molecules", reads = "reads", molecules = "molecules (UMI-collapsed)")
draw_units <- function(make, path_fn, w, h, show = TRUE, can_combine = TRUE) {
  first <- TRUE
  for (u in plot_units_for(params, have_mol, can_combine)) {
    p <- make(unit_members(u), u)
    if (is.null(p)) next
    if (show && first) { print(p); first <- FALSE }
    save_plot(p, path_fn(u), w, h)
  }
}
st <- load_settings(params$path_settings, samples_in_data)
settings <- st$used
range_table <- build_range_table(settings, measures$measure, primary)
timings["Load"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

`r nrow(settings)` samples have settings and are analysed. `r if (length(st$missing)) sprintf("%d samples in the data have no settings row and are left out: %s.", length(st$missing), paste(head(st$missing, 5), collapse = ", ")) else "Every sample in the data has a settings row."` `r if (nrow(st$excluded)) sprintf("%d samples are marked exclude and are left out of every analysis.", nrow(st$excluded)) else ""` Units analysed: **`r paste(names(units), collapse = " and ")`**. `r dup_r <- unique(as.data.table(range_table)[measure == primary, .(range_name, lo, hi, floor, max_peaks, manual_control)], by = "range_name")[, key := paste(lo, hi, floor, max_peaks, manual_control)][, if (.N > 1) .(names = paste(range_name, collapse = ", ")), by = key]; if (nrow(dup_r)) sprintf("**Duplicate ranges:** %s have the same bounds and settings in the settings file, so their results are identical; remove one of each set, or give it different bounds.", paste(dup_r$names, collapse = "; ")) else ""`

How each measure's ranges are defined: a measure with its own `analysis_ranges_<measure>` column uses ranges on its own scale; otherwise reads are selected by their **`r primary`** length using the primary ranges, and the metrics are calculated on that measure. The selection is not applied to the other measure's own length: in a `r primary` range of 40–50, a combined measure such as a sum can run above 50. Every length is in units of that measure's motif (a pentanucleotide tract in 5 bp units), and a combined measure whose tracts have motifs of different lengths is in bp.

```{r range_overview}
ro <- as.data.table(range_table)[, .(samples = uniqueN(file_stem), ranges = paste(unique(range_text), collapse = "; ")),
                                 by = .(measure, range_measure, range_name)]
dt_full(ro, caption = "Ranges by measure (range_measure = the length used to select the reads)")
```

## Experiment map

Each bubble is one combination of group and time, sized and labelled by the number of samples.

```{r experiment_map, fig.height=max(3, 0.35 * length(unique(settings$group)) + 2)}
has_group <- any(!is.na(settings$group)) && "group" %in% params$cohort_plot_by
has_time <- any(!is.na(settings$time)) && "time" %in% params$cohort_plot_by
# group_label is the key for group controls, so it always follows the settings
# group column; cohort_plot_by only changes how the plots are laid out
settings$group_label <- ifelse(is.na(settings$group), "ungrouped", settings$group)
em <- settings %>% dplyr::count(group_label, time)
p_map <- if (has_time) ggplot(em, aes(time, group_label, size = n)) + geom_point(colour = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), size = 3, colour = "white") + scale_size_continuous(range = c(4, 14), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = display_group) + labs(x = params$time_label, y = NULL, title = "Samples by group and time") + theme_bw() else
  ggplot(em, aes(n, group_label)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.3) + scale_y_discrete(labels = display_group) +
  labs(x = "Samples", y = NULL, title = "Samples per group") + theme_bw()
print(p_map); save_plot(p_map, file.path(plots_dir, "experiment_map.png"), 10, max(3, 0.35 * length(unique(settings$group_label)) + 2))
```

# Distribution statistics

```{r distributions}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
wide <- lapply(units, function(u) dcast(u[file_stem %in% settings$file_stem], file_stem + id ~ measure, value.var = "length"))
rt_by_sample <- split(as.data.table(range_table), by = "file_stem")
select_values <- function(W, r) {
  rm <- W[[r$range_measure]]; v <- W[[r$measure]]
  if (is.null(rm) || is.null(v)) return(numeric(0))
  v <- v[!is.na(rm) & rm >= r$lo & rm <= r$hi]
  apply_floor(v[is.finite(v)], r$floor)
}
dist_list <- list(); peak_list <- list()
for (u in names(wide)) {
  Wsplit <- split(wide[[u]], by = "file_stem")
  res <- apply_fn(intersect(names(rt_by_sample), names(Wsplit)), function(s) {
    W <- Wsplit[[s]]; rr <- rt_by_sample[[s]]
    out <- vector("list", nrow(rr)); pk <- vector("list", nrow(rr))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(rr))) {
      r <- rr[i]
      rm <- W[[r$range_measure]]
      n_total <- if (is.null(rm)) 0L else sum(!is.na(rm) & rm >= r$lo & rm <= r$hi)
      x <- select_values(W, r)
      # Too few reads in the range: counted, but no statistics (stray reads from another
      # sample or a PCR smear would otherwise give a modal length and a setpoint)
      few <- length(x) < params$range_min_n
      ds <- distribution_stats(if (few) numeric(0) else x); ds$n_used <- length(x)
      out[[i]] <- data.frame(file_stem = s, unit = u, measure = r$measure, range_measure = r$range_measure,
                             analysis_range_name = r$range_name, range_label = r$range_label, n_total = n_total,
                             too_few = few, ds)
      pk[[i]] <- data.frame(file_stem = s, unit = u, measure = r$measure, analysis_range_name = r$range_name,
                            find_modal_peaks(if (few) numeric(0) else x, r$max_peaks, params$range_peak_span))
    }
    list(dist = rbindlist(out), peaks = rbindlist(pk))
  })
  dist_list[[u]] <- rbindlist(lapply(res, `[[`, "dist")); peak_list[[u]] <- rbindlist(lapply(res, `[[`, "peaks"))
}
distribution_summary <- rbindlist(dist_list); modal_peaks <- rbindlist(peak_list)
meta <- as.data.table(settings)[, .(file_stem, group, group_label, time, is_control)]
distribution_summary <- meta[distribution_summary, on = "file_stem"]
timings["Distributions"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

## Reads and molecules in each range

Each point is one sample: how many reads (and molecules) fall in each range of the primary measure. The dashed line is `range_min_n` (`r params$range_min_n`): a sample with fewer reads (or molecules) than this in a range gets no statistics or metrics for that range (they are left blank, with the count kept in `n_used`), and a control sample below it is left out of that range's group setpoint. This stops a few stray reads – from a PCR smear, or from another sample through barcode cross-talk – from giving a modal length or an instability index, as in a range above the normal allele of a sample with no expanded allele. `r rc_few <- distribution_summary[measure == primary & too_few == TRUE & n_used > 0, .N, by = unit]; if (nrow(rc_few)) sprintf('In this run, for %s, %s sample–range combinations had at least one read or molecule but fewer than %d.', primary, paste(sprintf('%d (%s)', rc_few$N, rc_few$unit), collapse = ' and '), params$range_min_n) else ''`

```{r range_counts, fig.height=5}
draw_units(function(us, u) {
rc <- distribution_summary[measure == primary & unit %in% us]
if (!nrow(rc)) return(NULL)
# Each range labelled with its bounds, as in the other range figures
rl <- as.data.table(range_table)[measure == primary, .(range_text = if (uniqueN(range_text) == 1) range_text[1] else "varies by sample"), by = .(analysis_range_name = range_name)]
rc <- rl[rc, on = "analysis_range_name"][, unit := factor(unit, levels = c("reads", "molecules"))]
rc[, xlab := factor(paste0(analysis_range_name, "\n", range_text), levels = unique(paste0(rl$analysis_range_name, "\n", rl$range_text)[order(rl$analysis_range_name)]))]
# n_used: the count the range_min_n cut-off is applied to (after any floor)
ggplot(rc, aes(xlab, pmax(n_used, 1), colour = unit)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8), alpha = 0.6, size = 1.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = params$range_min_n, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30") +
  scale_y_log10(labels = comma) + scale_colour_manual(values = unit_cols, breaks = names(unit_cols), labels = unit_labs, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Analysis range", y = "Count in range, after any floor (log scale)", title = sprintf("Count per range, %s: %s", unit_title[[u]], primary),
       subtitle = sprintf("Dashed line = range_min_n (%d): below it a range gets no statistics or metrics", params$range_min_n)) +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))
}, function(u) plot_path(plots_dir, "counts_per_range", primary, unit = u), 11, 5)
```

# Group controls

**How the group controls are calculated.** Reads and molecules are handled separately, each from its own distribution statistics above:

1. **Which samples.** The control samples of each group are chosen by `control_sample_selection` = **`r params$control_sample_selection`** (`flagged`: the samples marked as controls in the settings file; `earliest`: the samples at the group's earliest time point; `all`: every sample in the group).
2. **One value per control sample.** For each control sample, unit (reads or molecules), measure and range, its **`r params$control_setpoint_metric`** is taken from all its reads (or all its molecules) in the range.
3. **One setpoint per group.** These values are combined across the group's control samples by the **`r params$control_aggregation_method`**, giving one setpoint for each group, unit, measure and range. `control_sd` is the spread between the control samples and `control_n` how many there are.

The read-based setpoint is used for read-based metrics, and the molecule-based setpoint for molecule-based metrics, so a sample is never compared with a control counted a different way. Where the settings file gives a manual control length, it replaces this setpoint for that sample and range (for reads and molecules alike).

```{r controls}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
sp_metric <- params$control_setpoint_metric
plot_ranges_c <- if (length(params$plot_ranges)) params$plot_ranges else head(sort(unique(range_table$range_name[range_table$measure == primary])), 2)
ctrl_pool <- distribution_summary[!is.na(get(sp_metric))]
if (params$control_sample_selection == "flagged") ctrl_pool <- ctrl_pool[is_control == TRUE]
if (params$control_sample_selection == "earliest") {
  if (!any(!is.na(distribution_summary$time))) stop("control_sample_selection = 'earliest' needs a time column in the settings file")
  ctrl_pool <- ctrl_pool[!is.na(time)][, .SD[time == min(time)], by = .(group_label, unit, measure, analysis_range_name)]
}
group_controls <- if (isTRUE(params$group_control) && nrow(ctrl_pool)) ctrl_pool[, .(
  control_setpoint = aggregate_controls(get(sp_metric), params$control_aggregation_method),
  control_sd = sd(get(sp_metric)), control_n = .N, control_samples = paste(file_stem, collapse = "; ")),
  by = .(group_label, unit, measure, analysis_range_name)] else data.table()
if (isTRUE(params$group_control) && nrow(group_controls) == 0)
  warning("No control samples found (selection: ", params$control_sample_selection, "). Only sample-relative metrics are calculated.")
timings["Controls"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
if (nrow(group_controls)) dt_full(group_controls, caption = sprintf("Group control setpoints (%s of the controls' %s)", params$control_aggregation_method, sp_metric), digits = 2)
```

`r if (nrow(group_controls)) sprintf("**How to read this.** One panel per group, for %s in ranges %s. Each point is one control sample's %s%s, and the horizontal bar is the group's setpoint, the %s of those points. Points close together mean the controls agree and the setpoint is well defined; a control far from the others pulls the setpoint and every control-relative metric of its group with it, so check it before trusting that group's results.", primary, paste(plot_ranges_c, collapse = ", "), gsub("_", " ", sp_metric), if ("molecules" %in% names(units)) ", read-based (grey) and molecule-based (teal)" else "", params$control_aggregation_method) else ""`

```{r control_plot, eval=nrow(group_controls) > 0, fig.height=4.5}
cp <- ctrl_pool[measure == primary & analysis_range_name %in% plot_ranges_c][, unit := factor(unit, levels = c("reads", "molecules"))]
gcp <- group_controls[measure == primary & analysis_range_name %in% plot_ranges_c]
if (nrow(cp)) draw_units(function(us, u) {
  cpu <- cp[unit %in% us]; if (!nrow(cpu)) return(NULL)
  ggplot(cpu, aes(unit, get(sp_metric), colour = unit)) +
    geom_crossbar(data = gcp[unit %in% us], aes(y = control_setpoint, ymin = control_setpoint, ymax = control_setpoint), width = 0.6, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    facet_grid(analysis_range_name ~ group_label, scales = "free_y", labeller = labeller(group_label = as_labeller(wrap_label))) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = unit_cols, guide = "none") + scale_x_discrete(labels = unit_labs) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = paste("Control sample", gsub("_", " ", sp_metric)), title = sprintf("Control samples and group setpoints,\n%s: %s", unit_title[[u]], primary),
         subtitle = "Points = control samples; bar = the group setpoint (a manual control length in the settings file replaces it)") +
    theme_bw() + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7), plot.title.position = "plot")
}, function(u) plot_path(plots_dir, "control_setpoints", primary, unit = u), min(40, 3 + 2.2 * uniqueN(cp$group_label)), 2 + 2.5 * length(plot_ranges_c))
```

# Instability metrics

```{r instability}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
setp <- distribution_summary[, .(file_stem, unit, measure, analysis_range_name, group_label, own = get(sp_metric))]
if (nrow(group_controls)) {
  setp <- group_controls[, .(group_label, unit, measure, analysis_range_name, control_setpoint, control_sd, control_n)][setp, on = .(group_label, unit, measure, analysis_range_name)]
} else setp[, `:=`(control_setpoint = NA_real_, control_sd = NA_real_, control_n = NA_integer_)]
# A manual control length in the settings file replaces the group control for that sample
# and range; a blank cell leaves the group control in place
manual <- as.data.table(range_table)[!is.na(manual_control), .(file_stem, measure, analysis_range_name = range_name, manual_control)]
setp <- manual[setp, on = .(file_stem, measure, analysis_range_name)]
setp[, control_source := fifelse(!is.na(manual_control), "manual", fifelse(!is.na(control_setpoint), "group control", NA_character_))]
setp[, group_setpoint := control_setpoint]   # kept, to show beside a manual length
setp[!is.na(manual_control), `:=`(control_setpoint = manual_control, control_sd = NA_real_, control_n = NA_integer_)]
inst_list <- list()
for (u in names(wide)) {
  Wsplit <- split(wide[[u]], by = "file_stem")
  sp_u <- split(setp[unit == u], by = "file_stem")
  res <- apply_fn(intersect(names(rt_by_sample), names(Wsplit)), function(s) {
    W <- Wsplit[[s]]; rr <- rt_by_sample[[s]]; sp <- sp_u[[s]]
    out <- list()
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(rr))) {
      r <- rr[i]; x <- select_values(W, r)
      spi <- sp[measure == r$measure & analysis_range_name == r$range_name]
      for (type in c("sample_relative", "control_relative")) {
        s0 <- if (type == "sample_relative") spi$own[1] else spi$control_setpoint[1]
        if (!length(s0) || is.na(s0)) next
        out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(file_stem = s, unit = u, measure = r$measure, analysis_range_name = r$range_name,
          setpoint_type = type, setpoint_metric = sp_metric,
          setpoint_source = if (type == "sample_relative") "sample" else spi$control_source[1],
          if (length(x) < params$range_min_n) { st <- instability_stats(numeric(0), s0, params$expansion_thresholds); st$n_used <- length(x); st }
          else instability_stats(x, s0, params$expansion_thresholds))
      }
    }
    rbindlist(out)
  })
  inst_list[[u]] <- rbindlist(res)
}
instability_metrics <- rbindlist(inst_list)
setnames(instability_metrics, "setpoint", "setpoint_length")
instability_metrics <- distribution_summary[, .(file_stem, unit, measure, analysis_range_name, group, group_label, time, is_control,
                                                modal_length, median_length, mean_length, sd)][instability_metrics, on = .(file_stem, unit, measure, analysis_range_name)]
instability_metrics[, `:=`(modal_minus_setpoint = modal_length - setpoint_length, median_minus_setpoint = median_length - setpoint_length,
                           mean_minus_setpoint = mean_length - setpoint_length)]
cz <- setp[, .(file_stem, unit, measure, analysis_range_name, own, control_setpoint, control_sd)]
instability_metrics <- cz[instability_metrics, on = .(file_stem, unit, measure, analysis_range_name)]
instability_metrics[setpoint_type == "control_relative" & control_sd > 0, z_score := (own - control_setpoint) / control_sd]
instability_metrics[, c("own", "control_setpoint", "control_sd") := NULL]
# Samples and ranges whose control setpoint came from the settings file, listed in the report
# with the group control it replaces and the sample's own value, so a stale or mistyped value stands out
manual_used <- unique(setp[control_source == "manual", .(file_stem, group_label, unit, measure, analysis_range_name, manual_control,
                                                          group_control = round(group_setpoint, 1), sample_own = round(own, 1))])
rb <- unique(as.data.table(range_table)[, .(file_stem, measure, analysis_range_name = range_name,
                                           lo = fifelse(range_measure == measure, lo, NA_real_), hi = fifelse(range_measure == measure, hi, NA_real_))], by = c("file_stem", "measure", "analysis_range_name"))
manual_used <- rb[manual_used, on = .(file_stem, measure, analysis_range_name)]
manual_used[, check := fcase((!is.na(lo) & manual_control < lo) | (!is.na(hi) & manual_control > hi), "outside the range",
                             !is.na(group_control) & abs(manual_control - group_control) >= 5, "5+ units from the group control",
                             default = "")]
manual_used[, c("lo", "hi") := NULL]
timings["Instability metrics"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

`r if (nrow(manual_used)) sprintf("**Manual control lengths used.** The settings file gives a manual control length for %d sample(s) and %d range(s); there it replaces the group control (setpoint_source = manual in the instability_metrics sheet). Check these are intended: a value left in the settings file from an earlier analysis also overrides the group control. The table gives, beside each manual length, the group control it replaces and the sample's own %s; %s", uniqueN(manual_used$file_stem), uniqueN(manual_used[, .(measure, analysis_range_name)]), gsub("_", " ", sp_metric), { nb <- manual_used[check != "", uniqueN(paste(file_stem, measure, analysis_range_name))]; if (nb) sprintf("**%d sample-range(s) are flagged** in the check column, with a manual length outside the range or 5 or more units from the group control.", nb) else "none lies outside its range or 5 or more units from the group control." }) else "No manual control lengths are given in the settings file, so every control-relative setpoint comes from the group controls."`

```{r manual_used_table, eval=nrow(manual_used) > 0}
setorder(manual_used, -check, analysis_range_name, file_stem)
dt_full(manual_used[, .(file_stem, group = group_label, unit, measure, range = analysis_range_name, manual_control, group_control, sample_own, check)],
        caption = "Samples and ranges whose control setpoint is the manual control length from the settings file")
```

## Timecourses by group

```{r headline_setup}
plot_ranges <- if (length(params$plot_ranges)) params$plot_ranges else head(sort(unique(range_table$range_name[range_table$measure == primary])), 2)
hl <- intersect(update_metric_names(params$headline_metrics), names(instability_metrics))
hl_type <- if (params$headline_setpoint_type %in% instability_metrics$setpoint_type) params$headline_setpoint_type else "sample_relative"
hl_labels <- c(modal_length = "Modal length", median_length = "Median length", mean_length = "Mean length",
               instability_index = "Instability index", expansion_index = "Expansion index", contraction_index = "Contraction index",
               mean_change_above_setpoint = "Mean change above\nthe setpoint", mean_change_below_setpoint = "Mean change below\nthe setpoint",
               expansion_ratio = "Expansion ratio",
               setNames(paste0("Share ", params$expansion_thresholds, "+ units\nabove the setpoint"), threshold_col(params$expansion_thresholds, "above")),
               setNames(paste0("Share ", params$expansion_thresholds, "+ units\nbelow the setpoint"), threshold_col(params$expansion_thresholds, "below")),
               share_above_setpoint = "Share above\nthe setpoint", share_below_setpoint = "Share below\nthe setpoint")
timecourse_plot <- function(d, title) {
  if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
  # One row per metric (each with its own y axis, % ticks for proportions), one column per group
  rows <- lapply(seq_along(hl), function(k) {
    v <- hl[k]; dd <- d[, .(time, group_label, unit, value = get(v))][is.finite(value)]
    is_prop <- grepl("^share", v)
    base <- if (has_time) ggplot(dd, aes(time, value, colour = unit)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 2.2) +
        stat_summary(aes(group = unit), fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 0.8)
      else ggplot(dd, aes(group_label, value, colour = unit)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA) + scale_x_discrete(labels = display_group) +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, alpha = 0.6)
    base + facet_wrap(~ group_label, nrow = 1, scales = if (has_time) "fixed" else "free_x", labeller = as_labeller(function(x) wrap_label(x, 40))) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = unit_cols, breaks = names(unit_cols), labels = unit_labs, name = NULL, drop = TRUE) +
      (if (is_prop) scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis()) else scale_y_continuous()) +
      labs(x = if (k == length(hl)) (if (has_time) params$time_label else NULL) else NULL, y = if (v %in% names(hl_labels)) hl_labels[[v]] else v) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 13) + theme(legend.position = if (k == 1) "top" else "none",
                         strip.text = if (k == 1) element_text(size = 11) else element_blank(),
                         strip.background = if (k == 1) element_rect() else element_blank(),
                         axis.text.x = if (k == length(hl)) element_text() else element_blank())
  })
  patchwork::wrap_plots(rows, ncol = 1) + patchwork::plot_annotation(title = title,
    subtitle = sprintf("Points = samples; %s.\nInstability metrics %s; setpoint = %s.", if (has_time) "lines = mean at each time" else "boxes = spread across samples", gsub("_", " ", hl_type), gsub("_", " ", sp_metric)))
}
n_groups <- length(unique(instability_metrics$group_label))
tc_w <- min(40, 3.5 + 3.6 * n_groups); tc_h <- min(45, 2.1 * length(hl) + 2)
```

The headline metrics for each group, plotted against time: one column per group, one row per metric, each row on its own scale. By default these are the modal, median and mean length, the instability, expansion and contraction indices, and the shares of reads at least 5 units above and below the setpoint (`headline_metrics` sets them; every metric is in instability.xlsx, and the noisier expansion and contraction ratios can be added). Length metrics (modal, median, mean) are the sample's own; the instability metrics are `r gsub("_", " ", hl_type)`. Reads are grey`r if ("molecules" %in% names(units)) " and molecules teal" else ""`. Shown here: **`r primary`**, ranges `r paste(plot_ranges, collapse = ", ")`. Every measure and range is saved as `plots/timecourse/{unit}/{measure}/timecourse_{measure}_{range}_{unit}.png`, where the unit is `combined` (reads and molecules), `reads` or `molecules` as chosen by `plot_units`.

```{r headline_plots, fig.width=tc_w, fig.height=tc_h, results='asis'}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
for (m in measures$measure) for (rg in sort(unique(range_table$range_name[range_table$measure == m]))) {
  d <- instability_metrics[measure == m & analysis_range_name == rg & setpoint_type == hl_type]
  # A range with no reads in any sample has no metric to draw
  if (!nrow(d) || !any(vapply(hl, function(v) any(is.finite(d[[v]])), logical(1)))) next
  lab <- range_table$range_text[range_table$measure == m & range_table$range_name == rg][1]
  show <- m == primary && rg %in% plot_ranges
  if (show) cat("\n\n### ", m, ", ", rg, " (", lab, ")\n\n", sep = "")
  draw_units(function(us, u) timecourse_plot(d[unit %in% us], sprintf("%s, %s (%s): %s", m, rg, lab, unit_title[[u]])),
             function(u) plot_path(plots_dir, "timecourse", m, rg, unit = u), tc_w, tc_h, show = show)
}
timings["Timecourse plots"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

## Instability index across ranges

**How to read this.** The `r primary` instability index (`r gsub("_", " ", hl_type)`) of every sample in every range, one panel per group: the x-axis is the range (as defined in the settings file), each point one sample`r if ("molecules" %in% names(units)) ", read-based in grey and molecule-based in teal" else ""`, with a box for the spread across samples. **What it shows.** How much the result depends on the range chosen. Where a range cuts through an allele's peak, or takes in a smear of short PCR products, its index moves away from the neighbouring ranges; a range that agrees with its neighbours, and where reads and molecules agree, is a safer headline.

```{r ii_by_range, fig.height=min(30, 1.5 + 2.4 * uniqueN(instability_metrics$group_label))}
ir <- instability_metrics[measure == primary & setpoint_type == hl_type & !is.na(instability_index)]
if (nrow(ir)) {
  # One label per range; a range whose bounds differ between samples is labelled as such
  rlab <- as.data.table(range_table)[measure == primary, .(range_text = if (uniqueN(range_text) == 1) range_text[1] else "varies by sample"),
                                     by = .(analysis_range_name = range_name)]
  ir <- rlab[ir, on = "analysis_range_name"][, unit := factor(unit, levels = c("reads", "molecules"))]
  ir[, xlab := factor(paste0(analysis_range_name, "\n", range_text), levels = unique(paste0(rlab$analysis_range_name, "\n", rlab$range_text)[order(rlab$analysis_range_name)]))]
  draw_units(function(us, u) { iru <- ir[unit %in% us]; if (!nrow(iru)) return(NULL)
  ggplot(iru, aes(xlab, instability_index, colour = unit)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8), alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~ group_label, ncol = 1, labeller = as_labeller(function(x) wrap_label(x, 80))) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = unit_cols, breaks = names(unit_cols), labels = unit_labs, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Analysis range", y = "Instability index (units)", title = sprintf("Instability index by range, %s: %s", unit_title[[u]], primary),
         subtitle = paste("Each point is one sample;", gsub("_", " ", hl_type))) +
    theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = if (uniqueN(ir$analysis_range_name) > 6) element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 7) else element_text(size = 8),
                       legend.position = "top")
  }, function(u) plot_path(plots_dir, "instability_index_by_range", primary, unit = u), min(40, 4 + 0.9 * uniqueN(ir$analysis_range_name)), min(40, 1.5 + 2.4 * uniqueN(ir$group_label)))
}
```

```{r instability_table}
show_cols <- c("file_stem", "unit", "measure", "analysis_range_name", "group", "time", "setpoint_type", "setpoint_length",
               "n_used", "modal_length", "median_length", "mean_length", "instability_index", "expansion_index", "contraction_index",
               threshold_col(params$expansion_thresholds, "above"), "expansion_ratio", "z_score")
dt_full(instability_metrics[, intersect(show_cols, names(instability_metrics)), with = FALSE], caption = "Instability metrics (key columns; every column is in instability.xlsx)", digits = 3)
```

# Comparing tracts

When more than one tract is measured (for example CAG and CCG), this asks whether a read (or molecule) whose length changed in one tract also changed in the other – for example whether CAG instability carries the CCG tract with it. Pairs are set by `measure_pairs`; by default every pair of tracts is compared.

```{r pairs_setup}
tr_meas <- measures$measure[measures$type == "tract"]
pairs <- if (length(params$measure_pairs)) strsplit(params$measure_pairs, ":") else if (length(tr_meas) > 1) combn(tr_meas, 2, simplify = FALSE) else list()
has_pairs <- length(pairs) > 0
```

`r if (!has_pairs) "Only one tract was measured, so there is nothing to compare." else ""`

```{r pairs, eval=has_pairs, fig.height=5.5, results='asis'}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
pair_stats <- list(); pair_bins <- list()
# The per-sample scatter cannot overlay reads and molecules, so "combined" in plot_units gives one figure for each
scatter_units <- if (want_plot("pair_scatter", params)) plot_units_for(params, have_mol, can_combine = FALSE) else character(0)
for (pr in pairs) {
  A <- pr[1]; B <- pr[2]
  for (u in names(wide)) {
    W <- wide[[u]]
    if (!all(c(A, B) %in% names(W))) next
    by_range <- list()
    for (rg in all_ranges_A <- sort(unique(range_table$range_name[range_table$measure == A]))) {
      rr <- as.data.table(range_table)[measure == A & range_name == rg]
      if (!nrow(rr)) next
      d <- rr[, .(file_stem, range_measure, lo, hi)][W, on = "file_stem", nomatch = NULL]
      d <- d[!is.na(get(A)) & !is.na(get(B))]
      d <- d[get(unique(range_measure)[1]) >= lo & get(unique(range_measure)[1]) <= hi]
      if (!nrow(d)) next
      d[, `:=`(a = get(A), b = get(B))]
      d[, `:=`(dA = a - median(a), dB = b - median(b)), by = file_stem]
      ps <- d[, .(n = .N, rho = suppressWarnings(cor(a, b, method = "spearman")), median_A = median(a), median_B = median(b)), by = file_stem]
      ps[, `:=`(unit = u, measure_A = A, measure_B = B, analysis_range_name = rg)]
      pair_stats[[length(pair_stats) + 1]] <- ps
      d[, dA_bin := pmin(pmax(round(dA), -15), 15)]
      pb <- d[, .(mean_dB = mean(dB), n = .N), by = .(file_stem, dA_bin)][meta, on = "file_stem", nomatch = NULL]
      pb[, `:=`(unit = u, measure_A = A, measure_B = B, analysis_range_name = rg)]
      pair_bins[[length(pair_bins) + 1]] <- pb
      if (u %in% scatter_units) { set.seed(123); by_range[[rg]] <- d[, .SD[sample(.N, min(.N, params$pair_max_points))], by = file_stem][, .(file_stem, a, b, range = rg)] }
    }
    # One figure per sample: every range of A in its own panel (labelled with its lengths)
    if (u %in% scatter_units && length(by_range)) {
      br <- rbindlist(by_range)
      rl <- unique(as.data.table(range_table)[measure == A, .(range = range_name, range_label = sub(paste0("^", A, " "), "", range_text))], by = "range")
      br[, panel := factor(paste0(range, " (", rl$range_label[match(range, rl$range)], ")"), levels = unique(paste0(rl$range, " (", rl$range_label, ")"))[order(rl$range)])]
      for (s in unique(br$file_stem)) {
        ds <- br[file_stem == s]; ds[, panel := droplevels(panel)]
        p <- ggplot(ds, aes(a, b)) + geom_jitter(width = 0.25, height = 0.25, alpha = 0.3, size = 0.6, colour = if (u == "reads") "grey25" else "#00838f") +
          facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free") +
          labs(x = paste(A, "length"), y = paste(B, "length"), title = sprintf("%s: %s against %s, %s", s, B, A, unit_title[[u]]),
               subtitle = sprintf("One panel per %s range; each point = one %s (up to %s per range), jittered by up to 0.25", A, if (u == "reads") "read" else "UMI-collapsed molecule", comma(params$pair_max_points))) + theme_bw()
        nc <- ceiling(sqrt(nlevels(ds$panel)))
        save_plot(p, plot_path(plots_dir, "pair_scatter", s, paste0(A, "_vs_", B), unit = u), 3 + 3 * nc, 2 + 2.8 * ceiling(nlevels(ds$panel) / nc))
      }
    }
  }
}
pair_stats <- rbindlist(pair_stats); pair_bins <- rbindlist(pair_bins)
timings["Pairs"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
for (pr in pairs) for (rg in sort(unique(pair_bins$analysis_range_name))) {
  A <- pr[1]; B <- pr[2]
  show <- rg %in% plot_ranges   # drawn here for plot_ranges; saved for every range
  ab <- paste0(A, "_vs_", B)
  # A sample's bin with only a few reads or molecules gives a spike that is noise, so the
  # sample lines are drawn only where a bin holds at least 5
  pb <- pair_bins[measure_A == A & measure_B == B & analysis_range_name == rg & n >= 5]
  if (!nrow(pb)) next
  if (show) cat(sprintf("\n\n### %s against %s, %s\n\n", B, A, rg))
  if (show) cat(sprintf("For each sample, every %s's change from the sample's median in **%s** (x, rounded, capped at ±15) against its change in **%s** (y). Each thin line is one sample; the thick line is the mean across samples in the group. Each sample's line is drawn only where its bin holds at least 5 reads or molecules. A flat line at zero means %s does not change with %s; a rising line means reads that expanded in %s also lengthened in %s. Reads and molecules are drawn separately; read-level co-variation can partly reflect PCR and sequencing error on the same read.\n\n",
              "read or molecule", A, B, B, A, A, B))
  draw_units(function(us, u) { pbu <- pb[unit %in% us]; if (!nrow(pbu)) return(NULL)
  ggplot(pbu, aes(dA_bin, mean_dB, colour = unit)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_line(aes(group = interaction(file_stem, unit)), alpha = 0.25) +
    stat_summary(aes(group = unit), fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 1.1) +
    facet_wrap(~ group_label, labeller = as_labeller(function(x) wrap_label(x, 60))) + scale_colour_manual(values = unit_cols, breaks = names(unit_cols), labels = unit_labs, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = sprintf("Change in %s from the sample median", A), y = sprintf("Mean change in %s", B),
         title = sprintf("%s change against %s change, %s: %s", B, A, rg, unit_title[[u]])) + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top")
  }, function(u) plot_path(plots_dir, "pair_trend", ab, rg, unit = u), 11, 5.5, show = show)
  ps <- pair_stats[measure_A == A & measure_B == B & analysis_range_name == rg][meta, on = "file_stem", nomatch = NULL]
  # Groups down the y-axis, so long group names are readable however many groups there are;
  # within a group, reads above molecules
  n_grp <- uniqueN(ps$group_label)
  draw_units(function(us, u) { psu <- copy(ps[unit %in% us]); if (!nrow(psu)) return(NULL)
  psu[, unit := factor(unit, levels = c("molecules", "reads"))]
  psu[, group_label := factor(group_label, levels = rev(sort(unique(group_label))))]
  ggplot(psu, aes(group_label, rho, colour = unit)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8), alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = unit_cols, breaks = names(unit_cols), labels = unit_labs, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) wrap_label(x, 40)) + coord_flip() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Spearman correlation", title = sprintf("Per-sample correlation of %s and %s lengths, %s: %s", A, B, rg, unit_title[[u]]),
         subtitle = "Each point is one sample; 0 = the two tracts' lengths vary independently") +
    theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top")
  }, function(u) plot_path(plots_dir, "pair_correlation", ab, rg, unit = u), 10, min(40, 2 + 0.6 * n_grp * (if (u == "combined") 2 else 1)), show = show)
}
```

```{r pair_maps, eval=has_pairs, results='asis'}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
# Each tract's length against the other's, read by read (or molecule by molecule), for all
# lengths: a 2-D histogram per group for the whole run, and one figure per group with a
# panel per sample. Reads and molecules cannot share one histogram, so "combined" gives both.
map_units <- intersect(plot_units_for(params, have_mol, can_combine = FALSE), names(wide))
want_run <- want_plot("pair_map", params); want_grp <- want_plot("pair_map_group", params)
lab_m <- short_labels(meta$file_stem)
for (pr in pairs) {
  A <- pr[1]; B <- pr[2]; ab <- paste0(A, "_vs_", B); shown <- FALSE
  for (u in if (want_run || want_grp) map_units else character(0)) {
    W <- wide[[u]]; if (!all(c(A, B) %in% names(W))) next
    d <- W[!is.na(get(A)) & !is.na(get(B)), .(file_stem, a = round(get(A)), b = round(get(B)))][meta[, .(file_stem, group_label, time)], on = "file_stem", nomatch = NULL]
    if (!nrow(d)) next
    xl <- c(min(d$a), stats::quantile(d$a, 0.999)) + c(-1, 1); yl <- c(min(d$b), stats::quantile(d$b, 0.999)) + c(-1, 1)
    what <- if (u == "reads") "reads" else "molecules (UMI-collapsed)"
    scale_share <- scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", breaks = 10^(-4:0), labels = c("0.01%", "0.1%", "1%", "10%", "100%"), limits = c(1e-4, 1), oob = scales::squish,
                                        name = sprintf("Share of the\n%s", if (u == "reads") "reads" else "molecules"))
    if (want_run) {
      tg <- d[, .N, by = .(group_label, a, b)][, share := N / sum(N), by = group_label]
      n_g <- uniqueN(tg$group_label); nc <- min(4, n_g)
      p <- ggplot(tg, aes(a, b, fill = share)) + geom_tile() + scale_share +
        facet_wrap(~ group_label, ncol = nc, labeller = as_labeller(function(x) wrap_label(display_group(x), 40))) +
        coord_cartesian(xlim = xl, ylim = yl) +
        labs(x = paste(A, "length (repeat units)"), y = paste(B, "length (repeat units)"),
             title = sprintf("%s against %s, every %s: by group", B, A, if (u == "reads") "read" else "molecule"),
             subtitle = sprintf("Each panel pools a group's %s; colour = share of them at each pair of lengths (log scale)\nAll lengths; the top 0.1%% of each axis is not drawn", what)) +
        theme_bw() + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
      h <- 2 + 2.6 * ceiling(n_g / nc)
      save_plot(p, plot_path(plots_dir, "pair_map", ab, unit = u), max(9, 2.5 + 2.8 * nc), h)
      if (!shown && (u == "molecules" || !"molecules" %in% map_units)) {
        cat(sprintf("\n\n### %s against %s, every %s\n\n", B, A, if (u == "reads") "read" else "molecule"))
        cat(sprintf("Each read's (or molecule's) **%s** length against its **%s** length, for all lengths, so the alleles, their spread and any link between the two tracts can be seen together. Each panel pools one group; the colour is the share of the group's %s at that pair of lengths, on a log scale so a minor population shows beside the main one. Samples with an expanded %s tract that also carries a different %s length show as a separate spot; a %s that changes with %s shows as a slope. Saved for reads and for molecules as `plots/pair_map/{unit}/pair_map_%s_{unit}.png`, and one figure per group with a panel per sample as `plots/pair_map_group/{unit}/pair_map_group_{group}_%s_{unit}.png`.\n\n", A, B, what, A, B, B, A, ab, ab))
        cat(sprintf("![](%s)\n\n", md_path(plot_path(plots_dir, "pair_map", ab, unit = u))))
        shown <- TRUE
      }
    }
    if (want_grp) for (g in unique(d$group_label)) {
      dg <- d[group_label == g]
      ts <- dg[, .N, by = .(file_stem, time, a, b)][, share := N / sum(N), by = file_stem]
      ord <- unique(ts[order(time, file_stem), file_stem])
      ts[, sample := factor(paste0(lab_m[file_stem], ifelse(is.na(time), "", paste0(" (t=", time, ")"))),
                            levels = unique(paste0(lab_m[ord], ifelse(is.na(ts$time[match(ord, ts$file_stem)]), "", paste0(" (t=", ts$time[match(ord, ts$file_stem)], ")")))))]
      ns <- uniqueN(ts$sample); nc <- min(4, ns)
      p <- ggplot(ts, aes(a, b, fill = share)) + geom_tile() + scale_share + facet_wrap(~ sample, ncol = nc) +
        coord_cartesian(xlim = xl, ylim = yl) +
        labs(x = paste(A, "length (repeat units)"), y = paste(B, "length (repeat units)"),
             title = sprintf("%s: %s against %s, every %s", display_group(g), B, A, if (u == "reads") "read" else "molecule"),
             subtitle = sprintf("One panel per sample, in time order; colour = share of the sample's %s at each pair of lengths (log scale)", what)) +
        theme_bw() + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
      save_plot(p, plot_path(plots_dir, "pair_map_group", g, ab, unit = u), max(9, 2.5 + 2.8 * nc), 2 + 2.6 * ceiling(ns / nc))
    }
  }
}
timings["Tract maps"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

```{r save}
module6_output <- list(settings = settings, range_table = range_table, distribution_summary = distribution_summary, modal_peaks = modal_peaks,
                       group_controls = group_controls, instability_metrics = instability_metrics, 
                       pair_stats = if (has_pairs) pair_stats else NULL, pair_bins = if (has_pairs) pair_bins else NULL,
                       excluded = st$excluded, hash = params$module_hash)
output_path <- file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "06_instability.RData")
save(module6_output, file = output_path, compression_level = 1)   # level 1: several times faster to write than the default, files slightly larger
write_excel_function(list(definitions = metric_definitions(params$expansion_thresholds), range_table = range_table, distribution_summary = distribution_summary, modal_peaks = modal_peaks,
                          group_controls = group_controls, instability_metrics = instability_metrics, 
                          pair_stats = module6_output$pair_stats, excluded_samples = st$excluded), xlsx_path)
fwrite(instability_metrics, file.path(ins_dir, "instability_metrics.tsv"), sep = "\t", na = "NA")
fwrite(distribution_summary, file.path(ins_dir, "distribution_summary.tsv"), sep = "\t", na = "NA")
```
